name: Round Manager
description: The match as a state machine: intro, fight, knockout, round end, match end, best-of-N scoring, and the round clock. It owns the lifecycle and the win tally because every other fighting component needs a single answer to 'is combat legal right now' — inputs during intro, hits after KO, and meter gain between rounds all key off the round state this publishes. It deliberately does not own the clock mechanism: utility.timer_system counts, and this component decides what the count means, including whether time-out goes to the higher-health fighter or a draw. It also does not own match-level stakes beyond the score — bracket position, wagers, and ladder effects belong to social.leaderboard and whatever tournament layer consumes combat.match_ended. Round resets reposition the fighters through movement.character_body; this component orders the reset but does not move anyone itself.

inputs.name: roundsToWin
inputs.description: Wins needed to take the match. Two is the genre default; one makes every round match point, three lengthens sets for tournament play.

inputs.name: roundSeconds
inputs.description: The round clock, handed to utility.timer_system. 99 is tradition; shorter clocks force engagement in zoning-heavy matchups.

inputs.name: introSeconds
inputs.description: Locked-out period before combat is legal. Long enough for the round callout to read, short enough that rematches do not drag.

inputs.name: timeOutRule
inputs.description: What an expired clock means: higherHealthWins rewards the life lead, draw awards no one. The rule is match design, not timing, so it lives here and not in the timer.

inputs.name: endOfRoundFreezeSeconds
inputs.description: Hitstop-style freeze after the deciding blow before positions reset. The beat that lets a KO land emotionally before the next round starts.

outputs.name: roundState
outputs.description: intro, fight, ko, roundEnd, or matchEnd — the fact every other combat component gates itself on.
